jobs.occupation: Working Student (d/f/m) Simulation Control UI Software Infrastructure (Ingenieur/in - Luft- und Raumfahrttechnik)
jobs.description:
About us

Airbus pioneers sustainable aerospace for a safe and united world. The Company constantly innovates to provide efficient and technologically-advanced solutions in aerospace, defence, and connected services. In commercial aircraft, Airbus offers modern and fuel-efficient airliners and associated services. Airbus is also a European leader in defence and security and one of the world's leading space businesses. In helicopters, Airbus provides the most efficient civil and military rotorcraft solutions and services worldwide.
Job description

In order to support the Simulation UI (User Interface) Systems department, Airbus Defence and Space is looking for a

Working Student (d/f/m) - Simulation Control UI Software Infrastructure

You are a full time student (d/f/m), looking for a working student position and want to get to know the insights of flight simulator development? Then apply now! We look forward to you supporting us in the Simulation UI Systems department as a working student (d/f/m) with approx. 18 hours a week!

- Location: Manching
- Start: 01.11.2026
- Duration: 12-18 months

Our department develops top-notch, high-fidelity engineering and training simulations for a variety of aircrafts, supporting the entire development lifecycle.

We are seeking a working student (d/f/m) in the context of control stations for our simulators. In addition to the overall simulation control & monitoring, these stations are used for instructing and debriefing complex military flight training sessions.

Definition working student

Working students are students who are enrolled at a University or some other institution of higher education, and who are employed in a reasonably long, fixed-term position parallel to their studies. This position must not be confused with an internship or with the possibility of writing a final thesis.

This employment usually takes place directly on the company's premises. A working student's main focus remains on their studies, which is why, during term-time, working students are not allowed to work more than 20 hours per week.

Working students therefore usually work near their place of study, so as to conveniently combine studying and employment.

Your location

Located about an hour’s drive north of Munich, Manching is an up-and-coming market town that offers a wide range of leisure and cultural activities. Here, you can enjoy the quality of life in the countryside while the pleasures of near-by cities are still within easy reach.

Your benefits

- Attractive salary and work-life balance with an 18-hour week (flexitime).
- Mobile working after agreement with the department.
- International environment with the opportunity to network globally.
- Work with modern/diversified technologies.
- At Airbus, we see you as a valuable team member and you are not hired to brew coffee, instead you are in close contact with the interfaces and are part of our weekly team meetings.
- Opportunity to participate in the Generation Airbus Community to expand your own network.

Your tasks and responsibilities

- Support development, maintenance and continuous improvement of the software build, integration and test toolchain.
- Contribute to the modernization of our dependency and package management infrastructure.
- Assist in enabling cross-platform software builds.
- Design, develop, test and maintain software by writing clean, efficient and maintainable code, and follow software development best practices. Analyze and debug software issues, and fix bugs.

Desired skills and qualifications

- Enrolled full-time student (d/f/m) in the area of computer science, or an equivalent field of study.
- Practical experience in the field of C++ software development.
- Knowledge of Qt/QML, Python and DevOps pipelines (CMake, Conan, Jenkins, …) would be an asset.
- Fluent level of English.

Please upload the following documents: cover letter, CV, relevant transcripts, enrollment certificate.

Not a 100% match? No worries! Airbus supports your personal growth.

Take your career to a new level and apply online (https://www.airbus.com/en/careers) now!

This job requires an awareness of any potential compliance risks and a commitment to act with integrity, as the foundation for the Company’s success, reputation and sustainable growth

By submitting your CV or application you are consenting to Airbus using and storing information about you for monitoring purposes relating to your application or future employment. This information will only be used by Airbus.
Airbus is committed to achieving workforce diversity and creating an inclusive working environment. We welcome all applications irrespective of social and cultural background, age, gender, disability, sexual orientation or religious belief.

At Airbus, we support you to work, connect and collaborate more easily and flexibly. Wherever possible, we foster flexible working arrangements to stimulate innovative thinking.

jobs.occupation: Lead System Engineer (m/f/d) for the NEW ATHENA-WFI satellite project (Ingenieur/in - Luft- und Raumfahrttechnik)
jobs.description:
The Max Planck Institute for Extraterrestrial Physics (MPE) in
Garching (near Munich), Germany, is a world-leading institute for
developing and operating state-of-the-art astronomical instruments.
Over the past years, MPE has taken a leading role in the development
of instrumentation for several international space- and ground-based
projects, for example XMM-Newton, Herschel, SRG/eROSITA, EUCLID, the
VLT telescopes (e.g. KMOS, GRAVITY) and Einstein Probe. The MPE
High-Energy group, led by Prof. K. Nandra, carries out major space
hardware programs including the development of X-ray detectors and
X-ray optics in support of its astrophysics research program. Within
the framework of ESA’s future large-class space mission New Athena,
MPE leads the international consortium developing the Wide Field
Imager (WFI), one of the two instruments aboard the X-ray satellite.
Further details about the WFI, which is based on the Max Planck
Society’s unique Silicon DEPFET technology, can be found here:
https://www.mpe.mpg.de/ATHENA-WFI/ The MPE High Energy group is
seeking an experienced Lead System Engineer for the WFI project, who
should in addition have in their earlier career stages been an
accomplished design engineer in any of the primary engineering
disciplines (electronics, optical, mechanical, control and/or software
engineering). As electronics forms the technical core of the
instrument, a design background in electronics engineering is
considered a particular asset. As the Lead System Engineer for the New
Athena WFI, you will be part of the Project Management Team. Working
as a senior member of the WFI team, reporting to the Principal
Investigator and the Project Manager, you will have ample
opportunities to innovate and develop new technical solutions. Lead
System Engineer (m/f/d) for the NEW ATHENA-WFI satellite project Job
Code: 18/2026 Your Tasks: Act as the technical authority for the whole
WFI instrument, establishing, maintaining and controlling the
instrument-level technical baseline throughout the project lifecycle.
Be responsible for the project's technical configuration management.
Work in close and continuous collaboration with the Project Manager,
Project Scientist and the engineering team. Requirements engineering.
Definition and control of technical interfaces (external:
WFI-to-spacecraft; internal: between WFI sub-systems), ensuring
consistency across all responsible sub-system teams. Application of
end-to-end systems analysis and modelling and the subsequent
allocation and management of technical budgets/​tolerances.
Definition of the verification requirements and success criteria that
integration and test plans must satisfy, in coordination with the MAIT
Manager. Support of system integration, verification and testing,
acting as the primary technical interface towards ESA and consortium
partners. Technical Management and Risk Assessment. Prepare technical
documentation for milestones and reviews, assist the Project Manager
with schedule development and resource planning, and monitor
engineering progress against the project schedule, coordinating the
technical actions needed to support timely achievement of engineering
milestones. Your Qualifications: Essential: A completed scientific
university degree (M.Sc. or Dipl.‑Ing.) in engineering or an
equivalent qualification with in‑depth knowledge of scientific
instrumentation development. A physics degree with applicable work
experience in instrumentation development will also be considered.
Desirable: Given that electronics is the technical core of the
instrument, prior design experience in electronics engineering is
regarded as a particular asset, though applicants with a strong
background in the other primary engineering disciplines are equally
encouraged to apply. A higher degree (Ph.D.) in System Engineering
would be an advantage. Knowledge and Experience: Successful candidate
is expected to bring proven systems engineering experience with
designing astronomical or other complex systems. Knowledge of:
Engineering management with a broad knowledge of the technologies
involved in the engineering activities being managed. Principles and
methods of systems engineering and requirements analysis. Technical
risk assessment. Modelling languages, and relevant software tools.
Characterisation methods to evaluate candidate design alternatives.
System integration, tools, test equipment, principles and methods of
validation. Knowledge of ESA design and quality requirements (ECSS
standards) is an advantage. Electronics design principles
(analogue/​digital, front-end and detector electronics) are
considered particularly relevant, given the central role of
electronics in the instrument. Skills: Very good communication skills.
Planning, organising resources, motivating people, measuring
performance and applying corrections where necessary. The ability to
balance technical, schedule, resource and contractual considerations,
and a clear understanding of when a technical decision needs to be
escalated — to the Project Manager or, in more significant cases, to
the Project Office. Fluency in written and spoken English. Fluency in
written and spoken German will be an advantage but is not essential.
We offer: A versatile, challenging and autonomous job in a dynamic and
culturally stimulating international research environment in the
development of satellite instrumentation. Interdisciplinary work in a
team of experienced engineers and physicists. Needs-oriented training
opportunities. Fair payment according to your qualifications and
professional experience in accordance with the collective agreement
for the public service up to pay group 14 (TVöD Bund). Company
pension scheme (VBL). Underground station U6 directly in front of the
institute. Canteen in the immediate vicinity. Reduced rates for
certain insurance policies. Free parking on the institute grounds. The

The Max Planck Society for the Advancement of Science (Max Planck Gesellschaft, MPG) is a self-governing scientific organization funded by the Federal and State Governments. It conducts basic research in the fields of natural sciences, the humanities and the social sciences in 85 institutes and research units in Germany and abroad.

The MPG consists of three sections: the Biology and Medicine Section, the Chemistry, Physics and Technology Section and the Human Sciences Section. Each section has a Scientific Scouting Officer who supports the respective section and its institutes in identifying the next generation of leading researchers.

For the Human Sciences Section, the Administrative Headquarters of the MPG are now seeking a:

Scientific Scouting Officer (all genders) –

80% part‑time initially, with a potential full‑time transition effective 1 January 2029

(Reference Number 63/26)

to start as early as possible.

The Section includes a range of disciplines, notably the History of Art, Anthropology, Demography, Economics, the History of Science, Law, Neurosciences, Political Sciences, Psychology, and Sociology.

Your responsibilities

- Proactive and systematic identification of outstanding scientists to support the Human Sciences Section and its Core and Appointment Commissions
- Building and analyzing candidate pools, generating appropriate statistics
- Using various talent acquisition tools, including but not limited to internet sourcing, data mining, social media, networking at national and international conferences, as well as other creative methods to identify outstanding candidates
- Analyzing candidate lists generated through nomination calls
- Implementing, maintaining and further developing candidate databases together with the two Scouting Officers of the other section
- Attending international conferences, participating in public outreach to promote the MPG
- Complementing the current scouting team and actively participating in constantly developing the team’s scouting concept, tackling human sciences-oriented as well as interdisciplinary scouting projects

Your profile

- Doctoral degree in one of the scientific disciplines of the Human Sciences Section and several years of postdoctoral experience
- Education and/or postdoctoral research abroad, ideally for several years
- In-depth knowledge of the German and international research landscape (including organizational and research-specific framework conditions)
- Proven scientific track record and demonstrated knowledge of the respective scientific community
- General interest in a broad range of scientific subjects covered in the Human Sciences Section and ability to quickly familiarize yourself with new areas of research
- Solution-oriented, service-driven, creative and open-minded working style
- Excellent proficiency in English (written and spoken, level C1–C2) and good proficiency in German (minimum level B2)
- Excellent interpersonal communication and networking skills, in order to interact with and coordinate partners with diverse professional and multicultural backgrounds
- Experience in working with AI applications or a willingness to learn how to use such systems
- Willingness to adopt flexible working hours, as well as taking part in regular business travel in Germany and abroad
- Experience in scouting/recruiting scientists would be desirable

Our offer

- You will gain fascinating insights into the outstanding research at our Max Planck Institutes.
- You will help to identify the next generation of outstanding scientists for the MPG by directly interacting with its leadership and directors.
- As a member of the Section Office, you will cooperate with the department "Institutes" at the Administrative Headquarters of the MPG.
- You will obtain an excellent overview of the entire spectrum of scientific administration and the structure of the German research landscape.

We are offering a payment up to salary level 14 of the collective wage agreement for the civil service (TVöD Bund) as well as various benefits.
This position is permanent and 80% part-time initially, with a potential full-time transition effective 1 January 2029. You will be based at the Administrative Headquarters of the MPG, located in the centre of Munich.

We offer a supportive work environment with flexible schedules, remote work options, and work-life balance. We invest in your professional growth through personalized development opportunities, health promotion programmes, and a company pension plan. Additional benefits include discounted public transportation passes and full access to standard public sector social benefits.

The Max Planck Society has set a goal of employing more people with severe disabilities. Applications from people with severe disabilities are expressly encouraged. The Max Planck Society is committed to gender equality and diversity. We welcome applicants from all backgrounds.

Have we piqued your interest?

If you are interested, please send your complete online application (https://cockpit.as-mediendesign.de/jump1/130734)  **(Reference Number 63/26)**, including a personalized cover letter, to our human resources department, indicating your possible starting date. We look forward to getting to know you.

Application deadline: 2 October 2026

About us We're a 65-person EdTech scale-up operating across Europe, on
a mission to help educators bring learning and belonging for every
child. Our AV1 robot is deployed across 19 countries with 5,000+
units, supporting schools to improve attendance, belonging, and
continuity of learning for children who cannot be physically present.
Consistently described as life-changing, it bridges the gap between
the student and their peers, restoring both educational continuity and
the essential sense of social belonging. The Opportunity — Marketing
Manager As a Marketing Manager, you’ll play a key role in bringing
our mission to life through the marketing campaigns: helping educators
bring learning and belonging to every child. You will be the decision
maker for our DACH and BENELUX campaigns. You will be responsible for:
Adapting and executing the global marketing strategy for audiences in
DACH and BENELUX. Driving marketing qualified leads from school
authorities and schools. Raising awareness of school non-attendance as
a growing challenge, positioning the AV1 robot as a trusted tool for
early intervention and school non-attendance, and engaging
decision-makers with compelling, evidence-based content. From crafting
case studies and coordinating national campaigns to enabling local
outreach and events, you will align marketing activity with Sales
goals and ensure every campaign is purposeful, measurable, and
relevant to the needs of our customers. What You’ll Do — Scope &
Responsibilities Marketing strategy & execution: Adapt and deliver the
DACH and BENELUX marketing strategy that aligns with the global
marketing strategy, local business objectives and the overall company
strategy. Contribute to the global marketing strategy from a DACH and
BENELUX perspective. Campaign management: Plan, execute, and manage
multi-channel marketing campaigns (including email marketing, content,
webinars, events/conferences and other tactics) to drive problem &
brand awareness and lead generation in the DACH and BENELUX markets.
Content localisation: Ensure that all marketing content and campaigns
are localised for the DACH and BENELUX audience while maintaining
brand consistency. Marketing Effectiveness: Oversee the marketing
budgets for your regions, ensuring all initiatives drive forward
marketing’s key performance indicators: Marketing Qualified Leads
(MQLs), Conversion Rate (from MQL to Customer) and Return on Marketing
Investment (ROMI). Performance analysis: Track, analyse, and report on
the success of marketing campaigns, using insights to optimise future
activities. What You Bring — Experience & Capabilities Strong
understanding of marketing principles, strategy, content creation, and
demand generation. Ideally from B2B tech or high-value education
products. Knowledge of the DACH and BENELUX markets – especially
Germany and The Netherlands – including customer behaviour, media
landscapes, and regional cultural nuances. Familiarity with marketing
automation tools, CRM platforms (e.g. HubSpot), Content Management
Systems (e.g. Webflow), email marketing tools and analytics software.
Proven ability to manage multiple complex campaigns simultaneously,
balancing high-level strategy with tactical delivery. Strong
communication and interpersonal skills (German and English business
fluency essential, Dutch desirable). Expert at analyzing performance
metrics to derive actionable insights and drive measurable business
impact. Autonomous and capable of taking initiative, while also being
an effective team player. Problem-solving skills with a creative
approach to overcoming challenges. A mature professional presence and
the ability to influence stakeholders at all levels. Why You’ll Love
it Here Purposeful campaigns: Your work keeps thousands of children
connected, learning, and included every single day. You can see the
impact you have with every child’s story. Autonomous ownership and
trust: As the main Marketing person for the DACH and BENELUX, you will
be given freedom to plan and execute whatever you see fit, as long as
it aligns with our global strategy and pushes the needle further. Grow
your craft: Elevate your skills in a lean environment, with freedom to
propose what you assess to be best practices and build on your
strengths. No bureaucracy: We are all pulling in the same direction -
there’s no space for bureaucracy or politics. Whatever supports our
mission, is what we focus on. Generous paid annual leave: You get 27
days vacation + public holidays. Mobile phone and Internet
subscription JobAuto car leasing Access to digital mental health
support service including free therapy sessions Annual company
get-together: Once a year we all meet up for a few days of connection,
socialising, and some truly memorable shared experiences. Additional
details Location This position is based in Munich with a hybrid
working model. You will report to our Global Marketing Director (based
in London) and work closely with cross-functional teams in Munich,
Oslo, London and remote. How to Apply Please click Apply and upload
your CV and a short cover letter in English outlining your motivation.
If you’d like, you can also include a short video (in English ) as
part of your application – this is optional, but it gives us a
chance to see a bit more of who you are beyond your CV. Let your
personality and passion shine! So if you want to own a marketing
function for the DACH and BENELUX regions in a company where your
campaigns empower schools to embrace true inclusion - this is your
opportunity, and we’d love to hear from you. You may watch how AV1
transforms inclusion in education here: vimeo.com/1098745115 You may
explore our mission and impact stories at noisolation.com We kindly
ask external recruitment agencies and consultants to refrain from
contacting us regarding this position.

About us At No Isolation, we’re a profitable, 65-person Scandinavian
EdTech scale-up operating across Europe. We help educators bring
learning and belonging to every child. Our AV1 robot is deployed in 19
countries, with 5,000+ units supporting schools to improve attendance,
belonging, and continuity of learning for children who cannot be
physically present. Consistently described as life-changing, it
bridges the gap between the student and their peers, restoring both
educational continuity and the essential sense of social belonging.
We’re established enough to have a proven solution and strong
financial foundations, yet still small enough for every new colleague
to have a visible impact on our next stage of growth. The Opportunity

- Account (Sales) Manager (m/w/d) We are already quite established in
Germany. With 1,500+ units already deployed nationwide with almost no
churn across strategic customers, it’s a proven, trusted, and loved
solution - used by teachers who need a reliable way to include absent
students, welcomed by families who feel their child is still
"there,” and embraced by pupils who can see, speak, and belong
again. The references are real, and the impact is repeatable at scale.
Our next chapter is expanding our footprint in Baden-Württemberg - a
strategic, organic expansion that extends what already works. It
represents a massive and vital opportunity for our mission. We’re
bringing the same quality, reliability, and outcomes that defined
success elsewhere, and we’re looking for a sales professional to
play a pivotal role in driving growth across the region. As Account
Manager, you will set your strategic focus, open executive-level doors
across education and public authorities, and orchestrate
multi-stakeholder decisions. Your craft is relationships: You’ll
cultivate a high-trust network across all your stakeholders - engaging
in person to move complex decisions forward. You will lead with rigor,
listen with empathy, and with executive credibility, you’ll turn
early wins into lighthouse references, and lay the operating cadence
that keeps momentum compounding year after year. What You’ll Do
Define and drive your territory strategy: Build and execute the
go-to-market plan for your focus area within the region -
segmentation, territory mapping, prioritizing key accounts, and
setting milestones that turn strategic goals into tangible outcomes.
Build strategic executive relationships: Build trust with education
authorities, municipal leaders, and school executives - map decision
paths, align to policy and budget cycles, and secure multi-level
sponsorship. Win and expand strategic accounts: Lead full-cycle
acquisition and growth; align executive sponsors, budget owners, and
procurement; run multi-stakeholder close plans to signed agreements.
Lead with consultative, framework-led sales: Combine solution selling
with proven methodologies (e.g., MEDDPICC, MEDDIC, SPIN, Challenger)
to pressure-test value, control timelines, and move from business case
to signed terms. Collaborate for seamless delivery and growth: Partner
with Customer Success, Marketing, and Product teams to ensure smooth
onboarding and implementation, capture outcomes, and turn success into
expansion and credible references. Create regional momentum: Build a
trusted partner network (associations, advocacy groups, integrators)
to accelerate adoption, and build visible presence by speaking at and
hosting conferences, roundtables, and policy forums to shape the
inclusion agenda. What You Bring New-business track record with
long-tail sales cycles (Germany): Solid B2B experience - creating and
closing multi-stakeholder deals, managing long cycles, and driving
consensus to close. Experience selling to the educational or public
sector will be a strong advantage. Executive relationship builder:
Ability to build credibility and earn trust from C-suite to school
leaders - advancing complex decisions through purposeful face-to-face
engagement and secure executive sponsorship. Strategic GTM & execution
discipline: Ability to build a targeted GTM strategy and turn it into
an operating rhythm - market segmentation, decision-maker mapping,
phased milestones, pipeline hygiene, and accurate forecasting
(HubSpot). Structured, consultative selling: Ability to run structured
discovery and build quantified ROI cases; experience with
methodologies such as MEDDPICC, MEDDIC, SPIN or Challenger is
beneficial. Language & location: Native-level German and professional
English; based anywhere within the Baden-Württemberg region. What We
Offer Proven platform: Expand within Baden-Württemberg with national
credibility, strong references, delivery expertise, and clear demand.
Territory ownership & autonomy: Own a key territory with significant
autonomy and decision-making responsibility. Growth & development:
Access to enablement, coaching, industry events, and opportunities to
help shape best practices as we grow in Germany. Tools &
cross-functional support: Work closely with Customer Success,
Marketing, and Product, with access to sales collateral, case studies,
and training. Scandinavian purpose-led culture: High standards,
meaningful work, and the freedom to do your best work. Highly rated
workplace: Engagement scores above benchmark, structured onboarding
with a buddy program, an annual company trip, and a collaborative
culture. Generous vacation: 27 days of annual leave plus public
holidays. Mobile & internet: Reimbursement for mobile phone and
internet subscriptions. JobAuto: Car leasing through salary sacrifice.
Annual company get-together: A yearly multi-day event focused on
connection, socializing, and memorable shared experiences.

Company Description About EIT RawMaterials As the world moves towards
a greener future, the demand for raw materials—minerals and
metals—is set to increase immensely over the next three decades.
Europe faces a critical challenge in securing a stable supply of these
essential resources. This challenge is where EIT RawMaterials steps
in. EIT RawMaterials is at the forefront of driving innovation and
sustainability in the raw materials sector. As an Innovation Community
within the European Institute of Innovation and Technology (EIT), we
collaborate with over 300 partners across industry, academia, and
research institutes. Together, we forge dynamic, long-term
partnerships to develop innovative solutions that meet Europe's
growing demand for raw materials. About the Role We are seeking a
proactive and highly organized Administration Specialist (m/f/d) to
join our HQ office. In this role, you will be responsible for
coordinating a wide range of administrative, operational, and
organizational activities that contribute to the efficient running of
the office and support a positive employee and visitor experience. The
ideal candidate is detail-oriented, service-focused, and enjoys
managing multiple priorities in a dynamic environment. You will work
closely with internal stakeholders, external partners, and leadership
teams to ensure seamless administrative processes and excellent
operational support. Your Responsibilities Office Management &
Administration Manage the day-to-day administrative operations of the
HQ office Ensure the office environment is well-maintained, organized,
and fully operational Coordinate office supplies, equipment, and
vendor relationships Prepare and manage correspondence, letters, and
official documentation Maintain records, administrative files, and
internal databases Support document management and filing processes
Meeting & Event Coordination Organize and coordinate internal
meetings, workshops, training sessions, and company events Manage
meeting schedules, invitations, agendas, and logistics Prepare meeting
rooms, materials, and presentations as required Coordinate catering,
external service providers, and event-related vendors Support the
successful execution of employee engagement activities and corporate
events Travel & Logistics Management Coordinate domestic and
international travel arrangements, including flights, accommodation,
transportation, and itineraries Support visitors and business guests
with travel and logistical arrangements Ensure travel documentation
and administrative requirements are completed on time Assist with
travel expense administration and reporting processes Administrative &
Operational Support Provide administrative support to management and
cross-functional teams Coordinate incoming and outgoing correspondence
and deliveries Support procurement and purchase order administration
Assist with invoice processing and vendor-related documentation
Contribute to the development and improvement of administrative
processes and procedures Stakeholder & Visitor Management Serve as a
point of contact for office-related inquiries Welcome and support
visitors, partners, and external stakeholders Coordinate
onboarding-related administrative activities for new employees when
required Foster a professional, welcoming, and service-oriented office
environment What You Bring Completed vocational training or degree in
Business Administration, Office Management, Hospitality Management, or
a related field Several years of experience in administration, office
management, executive support, or a similar role Excellent
organizational and coordination skills with strong attention to detail
Ability to manage multiple tasks while maintaining high-quality
standards Strong communication and interpersonal skills Proactive,
reliable, and solution-oriented approach Proficiency in Microsoft
Office applications (Outlook, Word, Excel, PowerPoint) Experience
working with administrative and procurement processes is an advantage
Fluency in German and English What We Offer A diverse and impactful
role at our HQ office An international and collaborative working
environment Opportunities to contribute to office operations, employee
experience, and organizational effectiveness Professional development
and learning opportunities Flexible and modern workplace environment A
supportive team culture that values initiative, collaboration, and
continuous improvement Application Process Overview The position will
stay open until a successful candidate is chosen. Application Review:
Our team thoroughly reviews each application. Please make sure to
submit your CV in English. Initial Interview (30 minutes): Meet with
the hiring manager and HR team. Second Interview (60 minutes): Second
interview with a presentation on a relevant topic to the hiring
manager and the HR team. Offer: If successful, receive an offer to
join our team.
